articles.originalTitle: Mexico is undergoing an architecture renaissance inspired by its ancient past - Wallpaper*
articles.title: Contemporary Mexican Architecture Draws Fresh Inspiration From Ancient Mesoamerican Roots
articles.excerpt: Writer and curator Su Wu examines the re-emergence of ancient Mesoamerican forms, motifs, and spatial principles in contemporary residential architecture across Mexico.
articles.content: A new generation of architects in Mexico is shaping a distinct design language by reinterpreting the construction principles of ancient Aztec, Maya, and other Mesoamerican peoples. A new book by writer and curator Su Wu documents how these ancient ideas are manifesting within private residential projects across the country. While Mesoamerican motifs previously appeared in large cultural institutions, their integration into private homes marks a shift toward deeply personal architectural efforts. Among the featured projects are Fernanda Canales's geometrically precise Casa 720 and Casa Bernal by Marcos Ruiz and Emmanuel Picault, which is oriented in relation to the Peña de Bernal monolith. Additional residential works highlighted include Juan O’Gorman's home for composer Conlon Nancarrow and a project by Pedro Reyes and Carla Fernández. Furthermore, artist Geraz Ato's hand-carved dwelling near Teotihuacán incorporates iconography and migration scenes referencing the region's ancient past. These residences demonstrate that Mesoamerican design principles remain relevant and active within contemporary private architecture.

articles.originalTitle: Getty Pitches In on First-Ever Conservation of an Earthquake-Damaged 17th-Century Church in the Andean Highlands of Peru - ARTnews.com
articles.title: Getty to Assist in First Conservation of Damaged Peruvian Church
articles.excerpt: The Getty is partnering with local authorities to undertake the first-ever conservation project on the 17th-century Church of Santo Tomás de Aquino in Peru's Cusco region.
articles.content: The Getty is working with local authorities on the first-ever conservation project for the 17th-century earthen Church of Santo Tomás de Aquino, located in the Andean highlands of Peru's Cusco region. The Peruvian government has allocated $5 million to a multi-year initiative to strengthen the earthquake-damaged structure and safeguard its collection of over 300 cultural objects, including 17th- and 18th-century paintings, gilded wooden retablos, and textiles. Construction is set to begin in 2027, utilizing the Getty Conservation Institute's Seismic Retrofitting Project methodologies. Among the notable works in the collection is a series of eight large easel paintings by Italian Jesuit artist Bernardo Bitti, created in Cusco in the late 1590s and previously thought to be lost. One painting from the series, "La Oración en el huerto," will be transferred to the Getty in 2027 for scientific analysis and conservation treatment. Experts note that the collection offers a rare research opportunity because it shows no evidence of prior restoration.

articles.originalTitle: Scholar Dishes About Finding a Long-Lost Caravaggio Painting in Paris - ARTnews.com
articles.title: Lost Caravaggio Painting Discovered in a Paris Gallery
articles.excerpt: Art historian Maria Cristina Terzaghi has shared details regarding a lost Caravaggio painting she identified in Paris.
articles.content: Art historian Maria Cristina Terzaghi has identified a painting missing for nearly two centuries in a Paris gallery as an original work by Caravaggio. Writing in La Repubblica, the Roma Tre University professor detailed her attribution of Young Man with a Carafe of Roses, believed to be painted in the 1590s. The composition features a young man alongside fruit and a water-filled glass carafe, with four earlier copies known to exist internationally. According to Terzaghi, the canvas appeared in a 1607 inventory belonging to Giuseppe Cesari before entering the Borghese collection, where records trace it until 1831. The trail later resumed in 1909 when a Paris bookseller's widow put the work up for auction as an anonymous piece. Terzaghi bases her authenticity claims on the quality of the subject's expressive face, the fabric, and the rendering of light through the glass carafe, comparing the floral details to descriptions by contemporary rival Giovanni Baglione. Questions remain regarding how the artwork traveled to Italy from France, and other specialists are expected to review the evidence. Meanwhile, another Italian art historian recently attributed a different portrait to Caravaggio.

articles.originalTitle: The Big Review: Krasner and Pollock: Past Continuous ★★★★½ - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Krasner and Pollock Exhibition Opens at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York
articles.excerpt: The Metropolitan Museum of Art presents an exhibition examining the artistic and relational ties between Lee Krasner and Jackson Pollock. The show remains on view until January 31, 2027.
articles.content: The Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York presents Krasner and Pollock: Past Continuous, an exhibition exploring the works of Lee Krasner and Jackson Pollock. Curated by David Breslin and Brinda Kumar, the exhibition examines the artistic interaction between the two mid-century artists while seeking to establish a primary focus on Krasner's output. The display juxtaposes Krasner's 1950s collage works with Pollock's monumental drip paintings within carefully structured gallery spaces. The curators emphasize Krasner's supportive role in Pollock's career alongside her independent experimental approach. The exhibition features eight collage paintings that Krasner originally exhibited at the Stable Gallery in 1955. Critics including Holland Cotter and Karen Wilkin have noted that the exhibition offers a necessary historical reassessment of both painters. The exhibition at the Metropolitan Museum of Art is open until January 31, 2027, with tickets priced at $30.

articles.originalTitle: Art Gallery of Ontario sets opening date for $73m new wing - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Art Gallery of Ontario Sets Opening Date for New C$100m Wing
articles.excerpt: The Art Gallery of Ontario in Toronto has announced that its new C$100m Dani Reiss Modern and Contemporary Gallery will open on September 25, 2027.
articles.content: The Art Gallery of Ontario (AGO) in Toronto has announced that its new five-storey, C$100m Dani Reiss Modern and Contemporary Gallery will open to the public on September 25, 2027. First made public in April 2022, the 40,000-square-foot expansion increases the museum's display space by roughly 30 percent, including 5,000 square feet of gallery spaces with 23-foot-tall ceilings. The new wing addresses the growth of the museum's modern and contemporary collection, which has expanded by about 18,000 pieces over the past decade, including recent acquisitions and gifts from the estates of Philip B. Lind, Peter Hujar, and collectors Carol and Morton Rapp. Sparked by a lead gift of C$35m from art collector and Canada Goose chief executive Dani Reiss, the project is now fully funded through community contributions and support from the governments of Ontario and Canada. Designed through a collaboration among architecture firms Diamond Schmitt, Selldorf Architects, and Two Row Architect, the sustainable building overlooks downtown Toronto's Grange Park.

articles.originalTitle: Oshinówò Studio tops Lutyens-designed war memorial with glass prism to honour Sierra Leone's Carrier Corps - Dezeen
articles.title: Oshinówò Studio Adds Etched Glass Pyramid to Historic Freetown War Memorial
articles.excerpt: Oshinówò Studio has extended a 1931 war memorial in Freetown with a structural glass pyramid dedicated to the Sierra Leone Carrier Corps.
articles.content: The Commonwealth War Graves Commission has unveiled a memorial dedicated to the Sierra Leone Carrier Corps in Freetown. Designed by Oshinówò Studio, the new structure sits atop a war memorial originally built by British architect Edwin Lutyens in 1931. While the initial monument honored soldiers who died in the first world war, it omitted the 946 members of the Sierra Leone Carrier Corps who perished while transporting supplies. According to studio founder Tosin Oshinówò, the extension follows the tapering geometry of Lutyens's stone monument, rising higher to display the etched names of the carrier corps members. Placing their names above those of the soldiers serves as a symbolic gesture of gratitude. The memorial project also incorporates a laser beacon designed to be illuminated on days of remembrance, projecting a column of light visible from up to 5 kilometers away. As part of the initiative, the 1930s memorial structure underwent full restoration by stone and bronze specialists.

articles.originalTitle: Matteo Thun designs Torre Velasca interiors using “the building itself as the starting point” - Dezeen
articles.title: Matteo Thun Completes Interior Design for Torre Velasca
articles.excerpt: Italian architect Matteo Thun has designed the interiors for 72 flats and common areas in Milan's Torre Velasca, drawing inspiration from the tower's original materials.
articles.content: Italian architect Matteo Thun has completed a comprehensive interior design project for Milan's iconic Torre Velasca, originally constructed in the 1950s by the BBPR architectural practice. Thun's studio designed 72 apartments across the upper floors, ranging from suites to duplex penthouses, alongside ground-floor common areas including the lobby, reception, and corridors. The design approach centered on reinterpreting the original materials and color palette of the skyscraper rather than introducing contrast. Original elements such as doors, windows, loggias, and bathroom tiles were preserved and juxtaposed with contemporary furniture and historic design references. Custom pink wall coverings in the living areas reflect the hue of the tower's facade plaster, while darker blue and green tones define the entrance and bedroom zones. The architect described the commission as a foundational lesson in architectural preservation and context.

articles.originalTitle: Is wood the future of urban architecture? - Wallpaper*
articles.title: Urban Architecture and the Expanding Role of Timber in Sustainable Design
articles.excerpt: Architecture studios are scaling up timber structures to mitigate global carbon emissions. Projects such as Wood City in Stockholm and a new development in Amsterdam highlight the expanding applications of wood.
articles.content: With the construction industry accounting for 37% to 40% of global carbon emissions, architectural studios are increasingly turning to timber as an alternative to conventional methods. Oskar Norelius, CEO of White Arkitekter, notes that timber architecture is no longer restricted to experimental, one-off projects, but is being scaled up for high-rises and large-scale developments. Wood City, a major development spanning 250,000 square meters in Sickla on the outskirts of Stockholm, is currently progressing through a 15-year master plan. The first block of the project utilizes a combination of cross-laminated timber and glulam. According to Norelius, while Sweden currently has an overcapacity of local timber resources, the primary challenge lies in the industry's risk aversion and the necessity for ongoing collaboration and innovation. The studio also recently won a development in Amsterdam comprising 500 homes across 20 buildings constructed from mass timber and biomaterials. Alongside timber, the practice explores bio-based materials such as hemp, clay, and lime chalk plaster, while integrating landscape architecture into its technical projects.

articles.originalTitle: How Going Blind Made Doris Salcedo’s Art Bigger and Better - ARTnews.com
articles.title: Collective Labor and a New Sculpture Woven From Human Hair
articles.excerpt: Colombian artist Doris Salcedo, who lost her central vision, prepares to premiere a massive hair-woven house in New York.
articles.content: Colombian artist Doris Salcedo altered her working method after being diagnosed with Stargardt disease at age 31 and losing her central vision. Transitioning from solo creation to collaborating with assistants, she found that collective statements yield more powerful results than a solitary voice. Scheduled for the White Cube Gallery in New York, her new sculpture features a full-sized house nearly 30 feet tall woven entirely from human hair. Dozens of assistants spent three years tying knots for the piece, which addresses global displacement and domicide. Salcedo previously focused on climate refugees at the Sharjah Biennial with Uprooted, constructed from 804 dead trees. In her latest work, pairing human hair with a house evokes the ties between bodies and buildings. Her studios also house teams working on finer details, such as meticulously removing starch from individual grains of rice to accompany the exhibition.

articles.originalTitle: Berkshire Glade by Turkel Design - Architectural Record
articles.title: Berkshire Glade Multi-Generational Residence Completed in Massachusetts
articles.excerpt: Located in the Berkshire hills of Massachusetts, Berkshire Glade was designed by Turkel Design as a multigenerational vacation home and future residence. Completed in May 2025, the 6,510-square-foot project comprises a primary residence and a guest house.
articles.content: Situated in the Berkshire hills of western Massachusetts, the Berkshire Glade project was designed as a multigenerational vacation home and future permanent residence for a couple with careers in New York and Boston. Spanning 6,510 square feet, the structure designed by Turkel Design overlooks a wooded hillside and Mount Washington. The design links two distinct volumes, a primary residence and a guest house, through a covered porch anchored by a fireplace. This layout balances shared family gatherings with individual privacy. The engineered wood structure relies on Douglas fir glue-laminated beams and thermally modified hemlock. The exterior is clad in Japanese charred wood known as shou sugi ban, which offers resistance to rot and insects. Wall systems, roofing, flooring, windows, doors, and custom cabinetry were fabricated as a package in a climate-controlled facility and shipped to the site for precision assembly. Built on a 120-acre site, the project reached completion in May 2025.

articles.originalTitle: Edgar Degas | Promenade beside the Sea | L819 - The National Gallery, London
articles.title: Edgar Degas's Promenade beside the Sea on Display at National Gallery London
articles.excerpt: Edgar Degas's 1860 early oil sketch Promenade beside the Sea, depicting the Bay of Naples, is on view at The National Gallery in London, reflecting the artist's early explorations of movement and equine subjects.
articles.content: The National Gallery in London houses Promenade beside the Sea by Edgar Degas, an early oil sketch produced around 1860. The artwork depicts an elegantly attired couple on horseback riding along the coast against cliffs beneath a rosy sky, with a gentleman in black and top hat alongside a lady in a dark riding habit sitting side-saddle. The location corresponds to the Bay of Naples, an area visited by Degas during trips to see his Italian family. Equine themes recur throughout the artist's oeuvre, and this piece represents an early exploration of movement through open brushwork. Although appearing as an outdoor study, the painting was likely created in his studio using preparatory drawings, including notebook sketches from Paris. Measuring 22.5 by 32.5 centimeters, the oil-on-canvas work is on long-term loan from the Gere Collection and is exhibited in Room 39 of the gallery.

articles.originalTitle: powerhouse parramatta's steel-latticed museum opens with art by es devlin and james turrell - Designboom
articles.title: Steel-Latticed Powerhouse Parramatta Museum Opens in Western Sydney
articles.excerpt: Powerhouse Parramatta, the largest museum built in New South Wales, opens in Western Sydney within a steel-latticed building designed by Moreau Kusunoki and Genton, featuring inaugural installations by Es Devlin and James Turrell.
articles.content: Situated along the Parramatta River in Western Sydney, the new cultural venue Powerhouse Parramatta opens to the public. Designed by Moreau Kusunoki and Genton, the building features two large volumes enclosed by a white structural lattice that enables expansive, column-free interiors. Spanning over 18,000 square meters of exhibition and public space, the institution stands as the largest museum ever built in New South Wales. The inaugural program presents more than 3,000 objects across five exhibitions. Among them are British artist Es Devlin's major presentation exploring human perception and nature, and American artist James Turrell's monumental light installation altering spatial perception. Additional exhibitions developed with OMA/AMO and other groups complete the opening lineup. The architectural project also incorporates waterfront public spaces, a landscaped square, a rooftop garden, and an observatory. A 23-day festival of performances and workshops accompanies the opening of the institution.

articles.originalTitle: About the Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires exhibition - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: V&A Museum Explores Byzantine and Ottoman Legacy in Major Exhibition
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum is hosting Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires, an exhibition exploring 1,600 years of artistic production from AD 330 to 1922.
articles.content: V&A South Kensington in London is presenting Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires, an exhibition spanning the period from AD 330 to 1922. The exhibition examines the art and design traditions of both the Byzantine and Ottoman empires, highlighting their creative legacy that shaped the Mediterranean and beyond. Spread across four main sections, the exhibition features over 200 objects, including rare decorative arts, fine silks, textiles, ceramic tiles, mosaics, precious metalwork, jewelry, sculpture, architectural furnishings, manuscripts, and paintings. The first section, Roman Beginnings, explores the refounding of the city in AD 330 as the capital of the Roman Empire under Constantine the Great, focusing on its infrastructure and the Hippodrome. Heaven and Earth, the second section, explores how art and architecture served Christianity. Power and Reach examines how the Ottoman court projected authority through visual spectacle and luxury materials, while the final section, Life in the City, investigates the city's cosmopolitan character, religious coexistence, and 19th-century shifts in style. The exhibition remains open until 9 May 2027.

articles.originalTitle: Best Government/Public Building: Essex County Wynona Lipman Family Courthouse - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Essex County Wynona Lipman Family Courthouse Wins Recognition
articles.excerpt: Built in Newark, the 266,000-square-foot, eight-story Essex County Wynona Lipman Family Courthouse consolidates previously dispersed family courts into a central location.
articles.content: Situated in Newark, the 266,000-square-foot, eight-story Essex County Wynona Lipman Family Courthouse consolidates previously dispersed family and children courts, probation services, and domestic violence units into a central urban location. The primary public entry is carved out under the upper floors to form a plaza as an extension of the streetscape. According to the submission, family courts require a de-escalating environment, addressed here by a multicolor art-glass two-story translucent screen on the public street wall and separate child-friendly playrooms in waiting areas. Constructing the massive complex in downtown Newark required meticulous coordination, including working within strict property lines, managing daily traffic flows, and minimizing disruptions to neighbors. The interior design divides spaces to separate hostile parties while accommodating sensitive zones, and integrates modern security with separate private entry points, holding cells, secure sallyports, and underground parking for judges. To counter unpredictable conditions, the project team relied on daily meetings and constant communication, allowing project managers, superintendents, and safety managers to address obstacles, coordinate daily tasks, and adapt in real time alongside cooperation with the city of Newark.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | Morocco Pavilion: DECLOSION - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Venice Biennale 2026 Morocco Pavilion Announces Declosion Performance
articles.excerpt: Scheduled for the Arsenale during the 2026 Venice Biennale, the Morocco Pavilion will present the performance Declosion, drawing on the cosmology of Hesiod's Theogony.
articles.content: As part of the 2026 Venice Biennale, the Morocco Pavilion at the Arsenale will host the performance titled Declosion. Drawing from the chaos narrative in Hesiod's Theogony, the performance invokes Clotho, the figure who spins the thread of life. Engaging in a dialogue with Amina Agueznay's artwork, the event explores the cyclical rhythm of existence spanning birth, life, and death. Featuring performer Inès Abergel within the installation Asǝṭṭa, the work reveals the transition from emptiness to fullness and nonbeing to being. Artistic support for the performance is provided by Amina Agueznay, with music composition by Guilain Delanoue. Movement advisors include Alice Dardenne and Romane Piffaut, while scenography is advised by Amine Slimani and Federico Urso. Objects for the installation are crafted by Malika Benmoumen, Mahdia Anoufr, Koltoum Gaddem, Khaddouj Alja, and Florian SôngNguyen. The performance is scheduled for November 21, 2026, from 16:30 to 16:50.

articles.originalTitle: Enthusiasm Remains High as Dubai Design Week and Design Doha Biennale Kick Off - WWD
articles.title: Dubai Design Week and Design Doha Biennial Kick Off
articles.excerpt: Despite regional challenges, Dubai Design Week and the Design Doha Biennial 2026 are launching with participants from over 50 countries, celebrating creativity and regional heritage.
articles.content: Despite regional challenges affecting trade, creative enthusiasm remains strong as Dubai Design Week opens its doors through November 8, featuring participants from over 50 countries. Anchored by the UAE Designer Exhibition under the theme Inherited Futures and curated by architect AlZaina Lootah, the event explores how inherited materials and rituals intersect with contemporary design. Key highlights include a collaboration between Yinka Ilori and Veuve Clicquot, Luke Edward Hall's immersive silverware experience for Buccellati, and workshops hosted by MillerKnoll. Additionally, designer Tristan Auer delivers the opening keynote following his appointment to lead the Burj Al Arab restoration, while Molteni&C inaugurates a new flagship on Jumeirah Beach Road. Opening Thursday, the Design Doha Biennial 2026 presents over 15 exhibitions featuring creators from the MENASA region and beyond. Fromm.Lab showcases 12 projects reinterpreting Arab heritage through contemporary design, and the Design Doha Prize announces winners across categories on November 7 at the Museum of Islamic Art, with an international jury led by India Mahdavi.

articles.originalTitle: Drop-in Design: Your Future City - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Designing the Future City Workshop at the V&A Museum
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum invites families and children aged 5 and over to design future public buildings using recycled materials in a free workshop.
articles.content: The Victoria and Albert Museum is hosting a hands-on town planning event for children and families in collaboration with architectural designer Jahba Anan and RIBA. At the V&A South Kensington, participants will imagine and redesign how schools, hospitals, libraries, and train stations might look in 2050. Drawing inspiration from the Design 1900–Now galleries, the program allows visitors to examine how design has transformed daily life over the past 125 years. Supported by the Adobe Foundation, attendees will use recycled materials to build mini models of their dream buildings and contribute them to a growing city model over five days. The free drop-in event is suitable for ages 5 and above, with all materials provided on-site. Visitors must ensure children are attended at all times. The venue offers comprehensive accessibility features, including baby-changing facilities, quiet spaces, and ear defenders available upon request from the Learning Centre Desk for families requiring sensory support.

articles.originalTitle: At High Point Market, Designers Celebrate a Major Theodore Alexander Milestone With AD - Architectural Digest
articles.title: Furniture Manufacturer Theodore Alexander Celebrates Its Thirtieth Anniversary
articles.excerpt: Known for its artisan roots, furniture manufacturer Theodore Alexander marked its 30th anniversary with a major celebration during the High Point Market event.
articles.content: Furniture manufacturer Theodore Alexander celebrated its 30th anniversary with a gathering during the High Point Market event. The entrance featured a towering 15-foot Chippendale-style Pentreath chair outside the showroom. AD PRO Senior Editor Mel Studach delivered opening remarks paying homage to company founder Paul Maitland Smith, who passed away earlier this fall at age 90. Attendees explored the showroom's four floors, including lower-level displays of new collections such as Voyager, Greenwich, and Heritage, the latter of which reintroduces archival Maitland Smith designs with refreshed proportions. Earlier this summer, the furniture maker opened a 40,000-square-foot flagship showroom in Manhasset, New York, featuring over 6,000 SKUs and highlighting the company's workshop artisan capabilities. Departing guests received a polished brass miniature replica of the signature Pentreath chair cast as a keychain.

articles.originalTitle: Human Unreadable Act III by Operator - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Operator Duo Livestreams Act Three of Human Unreadable at the V&A
articles.excerpt: Artist duo Operator brings the final act of their Human Unreadable series, examining human and machine agency, to the Victoria and Albert Museum.
articles.content: The Victoria and Albert Museum is hosting a livestream screening of Act III, the final act of the three-part work Human Unreadable by artist duo Operator, on 22 November 2026. Transmitted live from the Whitney Museum of American Art in New York, the multimedia performance examines negotiations between the body, ambition, and technology. The presentation utilizes 100 dance sequences from the Human Unreadable collection, woven together through scripted dialogue, performance art, lighting, scenic design, and an original score. Broadcast across multiple venues, the transmission features real-time editing from multiple camera perspectives. Commissioned by the Whitney Museum of American Art, the event forms part of the museum's digital art season exploring boundaries between human and machine agency.

articles.originalTitle: Morocco’s Design Renaissance Is Underway - WWD
articles.title: Moroccan Design Sector Revives With New Generation of Creators
articles.excerpt: Moroccan designers and creative entrepreneurs are reclaiming their heritage to secure international recognition and pricing power. According to government data, the country's craft exports are on the rise.
articles.content: A new generation of Moroccan designers and creative entrepreneurs is working to revitalize the country's craft heritage and secure broader international recognition. Government data shows that Morocco's craft exports reached 1.232 billion Moroccan dirhams in 2025, rising from 792 million dirhams in 2019. The United States accounted for 49 percent of these exports, followed by France at 10.5 percent. Organized by Hanane El Moutii, founder of the strategy firm Éclat, the inaugural edition of Morocco Design took place in Casablanca from October 5 to 7. The citywide program featured exhibitions, workshops, and showroom presentations that paired local talent with established international design brands. Industry participants note that while Morocco preserves centuries-old artisan traditions heavily coveted by the global luxury sector, local brands frequently face pricing challenges due to preconceived assumptions about lower production costs. Driven by both domestic talent and returning members of the diaspora, this growing movement aims to shift perceptions and establish long-term prestige for Moroccan creators. Preparations for the 2027 edition are already underway to expand cultural spaces and showcase more local creators.

articles.originalTitle: Marsden Hartley | Painting No. 50 | L1396 - The National Gallery, London
articles.title: Marsden Hartley's Painting No. 50 Reflects His Berlin Years
articles.excerpt: Created in Berlin between 1914 and 1915 by US artist Marsden Hartley, Painting No. 50 blends Native American cultural references with German military pageantry.
articles.content: Painting No. 50, a striking work by US artist Marsden Hartley created as part of his Amerika series after moving to Berlin in 1913, is on display at the National Gallery. Influenced by the militaristic atmosphere of pre-First World War Berlin, the artist integrated the choreography of street parades into his visual vocabulary. At the center of the composition, Hartley stacked simplified elements such as a teepee, a canoe, and a bow and arrow, incorporating black and yellow zigzags reminiscent of military insignia alongside concentric target-like circles. Although he had no direct contact with Native American communities while living in the United States, Hartley drew inspiration from popular culture and ethnographic museum collections in Paris and Berlin. This synthesis allowed him to align with the European avant-garde while simultaneously crafting a distinct American identity for European audiences. Due to wartime travel restrictions and rising hostility toward immigrants, Hartley returned to his home country in 1915. The oil on canvas composition is on loan from the Terra Foundation for American Art and is exhibited in Room 45.

articles.originalTitle: HISTORICAL ARCHIVE | The Pillar and Ground of the Truth by Pavel A. Florenskij - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Venice Biennale Stages Pavel A. Florensky Project at Historical Archive
articles.excerpt: The Historical Archive of La Biennale di Venezia will present a five-day special project dedicated to Pavel A. Florensky, exploring the relationship between language and truth. The performances will take place from 16 to 20 November at the Arsenale.
articles.content: La Biennale di Venezia is presenting The Pillar and Ground of the Truth by Pavel A. Florensky as part of the Biennale of the Word. Taking place from 16 to 20 November 2026 at the new premises of the Historical Archive at the Arsenale, the project is conceived and directed by Antonello Pocetti across five evenings. The texts have been adapted from Florensky's writings to convey the depth of his reflections. Each evening opens with contributions from figures in culture, philosophy, and religion, followed by staged readings. Born in 1882 in Yevlakh, Azerbaijan, Florensky studied mathematics in Moscow before turning to philosophy and theology. Ordained an Orthodox priest in 1911, he engaged in research spanning mathematics, music, painting, and philosophy. Following the 1917 Revolution, he remained in Russia, where he participated in scientific projects before being arrested on counter-revolutionary charges and executed near Leningrad on 8 December 1937. Tickets become available starting 29 October on the La Biennale di Venezia website.
